Repair of be-002. Verified against BlockEncoding.lean RegisterLayout (L14-18: systemQubits, signalQubits, pureAncillas) and auxiliaryQubits (L22-28: = signalQubits + pureAncillas, docstring 'pure ancillas that must be returned to a clean state'), plus BlockEncodingCost (L50-55). The corrected math is sound: workspace cleanliness on signal success is the ADDITIONAL promise that for every data input v the S=0 projection leaves |0>_S|0>_W (x) Tv with no S=0,W-nonzero component - this is exactly the 'must be returned to a clean state' obligation the docstring records, and it is NOT implied by the doubly-projected (S=0,W=0) submatrix. The rotation counterexample is valid: with 1-dim S and D and a workspace qubit R=[[cos t,-sin t],[sin t,cos t]], 0<t<pi/2, the doubly-projected block is the scalar cos t (a legitimate exact block for that scalar target), yet R|0> = cos t|0> + sin t|1> leaves the workspace dirty while signal success is certain. The cost point - both signal and pure-ancilla qubits occupy physical space (auxiliaryQubits sums them) and projection is not uncomputation - is correct and grounded in the layout/cost defs. CORE UNCHANGED (same auxiliary-accounting / clean-vs-flag semantics as be-002); the repair adds the explicit success-sector cleanup promise and the rotation counterexample. new_problem_core:false, alias:[qcb-core-be-002] correct. Prefixes correct. repair_admission:true.

Repair of be-010. Verified against BlockEncodingClassics.lean (sha256 matches 94ac6632...) matrix_mul_congr_pointwise (L792-797, pointwise equality is preserved by matrix multiplication) and productCleanBlockCertificate (L800-808, cleanBlock := Matrix.mul left.cleanBlock right.cleanBlock, blockProof := matrix_mul_congr_pointwise ...), plus productResourceCost (L831-836, auxiliaryQubits and gateCount ADD, depth adds). The corrected math is sound: with DISJOINT auxiliary registers each all-zero projection fixes its own factor and summing over the shared data index k gives sum_k A(i,k)B(k,j) = AB (exactly the Matrix.mul in the certificate). The X/X same-register counterexample is correct: 1-dim data + qubit ancilla, U=V=X gives each clean block <0|X|0> = 0 so the matrix product AB = 0, but the same-register composite <0|XX|0> = <0|I|0> = 1 != 0 - so reusing one register does NOT realize AB. The cleanup caveats are mathematically correct and are the substantive repair: resetting an entangled ancilla is non-unitary (can erase coherence) and applying V-inverse cancels V on the WHOLE state (erasing the desired action, not just garbage), so neither is a free coherent product repair; a different cleanup must be separately proved and charged. CORE UNCHANGED (same product-fresh-ancilla reasoning as be-010); the repair makes the disjoint-register product proof explicit and adds the X/X and reset/inverse counterexamples. ConcreteSemantics.lean (sha256 matches 454c0c5e...) orthogonal-failure-branch comment (L271-294) correctly cited as supporting the garbage-branch point. new_problem_core:false, alias:[qcb-core-be-010] correct.
